in writing. −the airport charges directive will put an end to longstanding discussions and disputes between airports and airlines over the cost and quality of air services. the new rules will also protect passengers from excessive airport charges and will put an end to the practice of charging exorbitant prices at large airports. in practice, the costs incurred by airlines in connection with the use of airports have so far been borne by consumers. the directive aims to increase transparency and the rules for the collection of airport charges. it also lays down more detailed rules on the quality of the services to be provided and establishes independent supervisory authorities. the new directive will finally make airport charges cost-effective and eliminate discrimination between specific airlines. the directive will apply to the 67 largest european airports, which handle more than 5 million passengers a year (including okęcie), and to the most important airport in a given eu member state. by 2010, the number of airports covered will increase by a further 10.
in writing. −between 2000 and 2006, there were 2.4 thousand acts of piracy recorded worldwide. except for the cases that the trucking companies don't report because they're afraid of higher insurance rates. according to australian government estimates, the true number of pirate attacks is 2,000 percent higher. piracy is causing losses of between 13 and 16 billion dollars a year, and that number could increase significantly in the coming years. somalia is just the tip of the iceberg. since 2000, the most dangerous areas in the world have been the coastal waters of southeast asia, as well as those of malaysia, indonesia, nigeria, iraq and tanzania. maritime piracy is not only a major threat to people, but also to maritime safety. the eu should do everything it can to combat this practice.
in writing. −international financial reporting standards (ifrss) provide a good foundation for the harmonisation of accounting standards worldwide. the widespread use of globally accepted accounting standards will improve the transparency and comparability of financial statements. it will benefit both businesses and investors. the united states shall only recognise financial statements prepared in accordance with ifrs as issued by the international accounting standards board (iasb). however, the united states agrees to a short transition period during which the financial statements prepared under ifrs as adopted under european community regulation no 1606/2002 will be accepted without the need for adjustment.
in writing. −on 19 may 2008, the european ombudsman, nikiforos diamandouros, presented his report to the committee on petitions. in it, he gave a detailed account of his activities, giving figures and percentages. the report shows that the number of admissible complaints lodged with the ombudsman increased from 449 in 2006 to 518 in 2007. last year, the number of inadmissible complaints decreased compared to 2006. the complaints were based on a variety of grounds: lack of transparency, refusal to provide information, abuse of power, inadequate procedures, unjustified delay, discrimination, negligence, legal errors. the european commission received the highest number of complaints (64%). only 9% of the requests addressed to the ombudsman concerned the european parliament. the european ombudsman also draws attention to the failings of the european institutions. mr diamandouros criticised the european commission for not publishing in 2006 the legally required 2005 annual report on access to european parliament, council and commission documents.

the next item is the report drawn up on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs by astrid lulling on the proposal for a council directive on the general conditions for excise duty (com (2008) 0078 - c6-0099/2008 - 2008/0051 (cns)) (a6-0417/2008).
member of the commission. − mr president, let me first of all thank the rapporteur mrs lulling and the econ committee for the report and the speedy treatment of this proposal, which provides the legal basis for the computerisation of excise procedures as of april 2010. member states as well as the commission have invested a lot in the excise movement control system (emcs). it replaces the current paper-based movement monitoring system with a new computerised one. the greater use of trans-european networks for communication between traders and excise authorities, and between excise authorities themselves, will reduce the time needed for the discharge of tax liability for excise movements. this will provide excise authorities with an essential tool to effectively address fraud and hence protect legitimate trade. at the same time, it will improve the services to taxpayers who will benefit from improved legal certainty and real-time information exchanges with their tax authorities. apart from these new provisions, the proposed directive will entirely recast and update the old horizontal excise directive of 1992. it will simplify and modernise the excise procedures, with the aim of reducing excise obligations for traders, in particular for traders carrying out cross-border business, without compromising excise controls. clearly, as the commission had proposed a new and up-to-date legal framework for excise, some of the more political issues included in this legislation had to be re-discussed. this concerns the issues of land-based tax-free shops, the position of transit airports and the maintaining of guide levels to distinguish commercial excise movements from movements of excise goods for personal use. many amendments proposed by parliament already conform to the text of the general orientation agreed in the ecofin meeting of 4 november 2008, or go in the same direction. they are also acceptable to the commission. i am therefore confident that the proposal can be adopted soon and that the timely application of the emcs is ensured.

now in the present treaty, in article 119, which has been the legal basis used by the commission, after many years of being rendered useless or not being used, to rely on it to come to the aid of a state which needed help, which needed urgent help, as was the case with hungary. the article in the treaty is developed in a regulation of 2002, which is the regulation we used for hungary and which is the regulation we are now also proposing to reform, as regards the ceiling on the amounts that can be made available, in order to help states in difficulty of this kind. yesterday we were vice-president of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in 1988 the commission had proposed a directive on the minimum level of alcohol permitted for drivers, but in the absence of agreement between the member states and the commission, the commission had to content itself with adopting a recommendation on 17 january 2001 to impose a maximum level of 0.5 mg/ml in all the member states. today, only three countries in the european union, ireland, malta and the united kingdom, have a maximum blood alcohol level above this value. the commission's recommendation also provided for a reduction in the blood alcohol level to 0.2 mg/ml for certain categories of drivers, including novice drivers, who are the subject of the first question raised by the honourable member. it is precisely novice drivers who are the main victims of road safety and it is therefore essential to reduce as far as possible the risk factors affecting them, for example by authorizing a blood alcohol level for this category not exceeding, as i have said, 0.2 mg/ml. this is in fact linked to the so-called zero rate measure, which was envisaged for this category of drivers in the communication adopted by the commission in october 2006 and which sets out a strategy to support member states in reducing alcohol-related harm. in view of this, ladies and gentlemen, the commission regrets that it does not believe that the political conditions exist for the member states to adopt legislation to further harmonise the alcohol content allowed in our union. the commission is not going to stand by vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i wish to begin by thanking ms gräßle for her energetic drive in this matter and the committee on budgetary control for forcefully carrying through the debate. the commission appreciates the considerable work of the rapporteur, who was instrumental in taking up this proposal, pending since 2006. a first proposal had already been made in 2004. times have changed since 2004 and 2006. the largest part of olaf’s work now is not with the institutions but with external parties, conducting anti-fraud investigations throughout europe and indeed throughout the world, wherever eu funds are spent. it has great success in this work, as is widely recognised. what remains is a schizophrenic situation, if you allow that analytical term: on the one hand olaf is a ‘normal’ commission directorate general, for which the commission has full responsibility; on the other hand, it is an investigative function, fully independent in its operations, but for which the commission is also held responsible. where are the limitations, and where are the limits of independence and accountability in such a set-up? it is our view that with the necessary independence from outside interference of a credible anti-fraud service comes the need for a clear and strong governance set-up. clear rules for investigations and strong accountability arrangements are the mirror of operational independence. there are basically only two options: olaf as part of the commission, but with clear allocation and separation of responsibility, or make olaf entirely independent from any eu institution and ensure separate strong oversight and accountability. the guiding principles behind the commission’s 2006 proposal were to strengthen the existing olaf legal framework: a clearer governance set-up for olaf; reinforced accountability and oversight; reinforced protection of persons under investigation and a reinforced framework for investigations and their follow-up. on that basis, the commission can fully support the amendments proposed in the draft report you are voting on today that are in line with the broad objectives of reform, and can thank you for those developed further. on the other hand, the commission made it very clear throughout the drafting process that some amendments cannot be taken into account in the current situation, simply because olaf’s present status as a commission directorate-general does not legally permit such changes. this includes, for example: olaf concluding independent cooperation agreements; olaf’s independent appearance before the european court of justice; or the european parliament and the council deciding on olaf directorate-general appointments. the commission also made clear that it cannot accept a limited number of proposals which, in their current wording, would depart from the governance improvements envisaged or would remove safeguards contained in the current regulation. this covers, for example, the scope of the governance framework, the procedural rights of persons concerned or a more effective follow-up of minor cases. however, the commission took careful note that, in parallel to the discussion of the current reform proposal, both the european parliament and the council repeatedly, and in a particularly insistent manner, stressed their preference for further simplification and consolidation of the entire complex of anti-fraud legislation. the upcoming czech presidency asked the commission to present a concept paper on that in time for a working-level discussion scheduled during the latter part of its mandate. the commission is therefore striving to present the requested broad reflection paper in early 2009, based on past experience with the existing anti-fraud set-up and the input from the current reform discussion, as well as any other useful elements, as sketched out above. the european parliament will be fully involved in that. let me conclude by stressing again that the commission is thankful for the support from the european parliament. the commission is not shying away from openly saying where, in our view, the limits are, but the commission has been, and will remain, ready to discuss in a spirit of full transparency and cooperation all issues necessary to designing a strong and credible framework for the future of olaf and a successful fight against fraud.
on behalf of the uen group. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: our debate comes on the eve of the 10th anniversary of olaf. the european anti-fraud office was created from the ruins of the disgraced, corrupt and nepotist commission headed by jacques santerra. life has shown that olaf is essential for the smooth functioning of the union's administration, but its very existence and operation is also a signal to the public opinion of the member states of the union that the bodies of the european union are under constant surveillance, control and scrutiny. the work of olaf in itself enhances the prestige of the european institutions. the work that is now being carried out, which is already well advanced, is intended to strengthen olaf's role in practice by: firstly, improving its working conditions; secondly, improving the quality of its operations; and thirdly, as my predecessors have said, strengthening its independence (thank you to the rapporteur on this occasion). this has been going on for four years. the european commission was the initiator, following the unfortunate experience of being forced to resign nine years ago. the document setting out olaf's new framework was consulted by the council of the union, the court of auditors, the data protection inspectorate, but also, and importantly, by a public hearing, which sought to engage public opinion. it was the conclusions of this public hearing and the court's special report that brought about the major changes to the original proposals four years ago. for example, it has been necessary to clarify the issues of olaf's cooperation with the member states of the union and with the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the european union. the key issue is to increase olaf's independence in a meaningful way. its staff must be completely independent in the performance of their duties. in the case of olaf investigations into the distribution of union funds, both to member states and to external assistance, the participation of the third countries and international organisations concerned in the course of olaf's activities should be guaranteed. in order to speed up olaf's work, it should be ensured that the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies grant olaf immediate and automatic access to databases concerning the management of european union funds and to any databases and relevant information. it's like a counter-culture that's been around for a while, where these very institutions have been hermetically sealed off from scrutiny. member states cannot treat olaf as an enemy or an unnecessary institution. each country of the union should designate the authorities of its administration which will cooperate with olaf on an ongoing basis. as you know, not all of our 27 member states have set up specialised services responsible for coordinating the fight against fraud at national level in the area of eu funds. close cooperation between olaf and europol and between olaf and eurojust is necessary. olaf must also be very transparent, including in its investigative procedure, procedural guarantees, the control of the legality of investigative activities and appeal procedures for suspects or those who may become suspects at a rapid pace. in the case of procedures concerning member states, controls may be carried out by representatives of those member states. they may be attended by representatives of the judiciary and duly involved in the olaf structure. that's what the amendments say. i am also against excessive sanctions against officials of the european institutions who allow themselves to make unauthorised disclosures about individual offices and potential corrupt practices. the case of our colleague, mr van buitenen, now an mep and formerly an official of the european commission, shows that in the past, repression has been directed not against those who committed abuses but against those who tried to identify, track and expose them. let this experience also serve as a warning when it comes to specific provisions on penalties and sanctions for officials who disclose information without authorisation. finally, citizens of the member states often overly identify corruption and abuse with the european institutions. to counteract this, there is a need for greater transparency in the work of the union's institutions, but also for much better information on the investigations carried out, on the methods by which the union actually combats corruption. hiding this information under the pretext that talking about it will lower the prestige of the union is a serious mistake. on the contrary, we must make these matters public so that the citizens and taxpayers of the european union know that theft is not shamefully swept under the carpet in our country.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i am very happy to be presenting my green credentials in addition to my anti-fraud credentials, so changing topics is also a pleasure. i would like to thank the european parliament for this discussion on the very important topic of environmental inspections. recognising the need for eu-wide action, parliament and the council adopted the recommendation on environmental inspections in 2001. the objective was to lay down common criteria for environmental inspections in order to ensure a better and more consistent implementation of environmental legislation through the community. at the time there was a long discussion on whether these criteria should be binding or non-binding. as a compromise, a non-binding recommendation was adopted. member states pledged to implement it fully and the commission was asked to review this decision on the basis of the experience with the implementation of the recommendation by the member states. the commission launched the review process with its communication of november 2007. in this communication the commission concluded that, although the recommendation has led to improvements in environmental inspections in some member states, it has unfortunately not been fully implemented in all member states. the commission thus put forward its preliminary views on how the situation could be improved. the measures that we deem necessary are: firstly, a modification of the recommendation to make it stronger and clearer, including a better reporting mechanism; secondly, where necessary, to complement the recommendation with legally binding inspection requirements in individual directives; and thirdly, to continue supporting the exchange of information and best practice between inspectorates in the context of impel. the commission is now gathering the input of the other institutions and of stakeholders on these initial proposals and will then present its final proposals. now, coming to the questions raised, i would like to make the following remarks. firstly, i would like to clarify that the views presented in the commission’s communication of november 2007 do not exclude the possibility of the commission presenting a proposal for a directive on environmental inspections in the future. the commission’s view, as expressed in its communication, is that there is a need for eu-wide legally binding rules to ensure effective environmental inspections. in that respect we have the same position as parliament. the question is, however, whether such rules should be horizontal and cover all environmental inspections or whether they should be sectoral and apply to specific installations or activities. both of these approaches have their advantages and disadvantages. a horizontal approach would be simpler and quicker to put in place. on the other hand, the sectoral approach would enable us to better address the specific aspects of the different installations or activities. for instance, the requirements for inspections of waste shipments are completely different from those for the inspection of industrial installations. by being more targeted we could set more effective requirements. to some extent, the sectoral approach is the one that we have already been practising for several years. for example, in the seveso ii directive, we have provisions on inspections of installations in order to prevent accidents. these provisions have proven to be very successful. we have now included inspection requirements in our proposal to revise the ippc directive. another sector where we see the need for further action is the implementation of the eu waste shipment regulation. the growing problem of illegal waste shipments is a risk for human health and the environment. there is clear evidence of illegal shipments recorded during joint eu waste shipment inspections coordinated by impel. recent trade data and studies on the export of certain waste streams, in particular electrical and electronic waste and end-of-life vehicles, indicate that significant volumes leave the eu. in many cases these shipments seem to violate the eu waste shipment regulation’s export bans. serious incidents of eu exports for dumping of waste in developing countries, such as the côte d’ivoire incident in 2006, as well as a recent greenpeace report about waste illegally shipped to west africa, underline the severity of the problem. the commission is currently examining the need for additional initiatives, including improved legislative requirements, in order to further and strengthen the inspections and controls of waste shipments. as we stated in our communication, we also see a need to establish common definitions for terms that are relevant for inspections. for this purpose we think that a horizontal recommendation would be an appropriate instrument. as regards the idea of transforming impel into an eu environmental inspection force, impel was created as an informal network of member states’ inspection authorities. its objective is to facilitate exchange of information and best practice between the people who are actually applying environmental legislation in the member states. i think we should preserve this role of impel of bringing together the expertise of inspectors and allowing for an informal exchange of ideas at european level. from the commission’s side we will continue our support to impel and reinforce our successful cooperation. this year impel was transformed from an informal network into an international association. this will not only give impel more visibility but also open new possibilities of activities for impel. to go further and create an eu environmental inspection force with powers of entry and powers to refer member states to the court of justice is an interesting and ambitious idea. however, it would raise important legal and institutional questions. we should also look at the instruments for the improvement of the enforcement of eu environmental legislation at our disposal at present and consider whether these could be further developed or put to better use. for example, the horizontal infringement cases that the commission launched against member states for systematic failure to enforce certain obligations, such as for the presence of thousands of illegal landfills in some member states, have led to the establishment of improved enforcement strategies in the member states. another example of an initiative that has led to better enforcement is the joint inspections of waste shipments throughout the community organised within the framework of impel with the support of the commission. we would consider ways to reinforce this cooperation and encourage all member states to participate in it.

madam president! i share the european commission's view that there are wide disparities in the way environmental controls are carried out in the member states, which makes it impossible to ensure the consistent implementation and enforcement of community law. in my parliamentary work, i had the opportunity to see the results of several projects carried out within the impel network, including the project on the control of transboundary movements of waste through seaports. i have found that the cooperation of the inspection services within the impel network is not only an exchange of experience but also, and perhaps above all, a joint inspection and exchange of information on environmental crimes and offences. some dishonest traders knowingly move their illegal activities to countries where they know that the control system is weaker and they can operate with impunity. if the control systems in all member states were uniform, such practices would not take place. this is another argument for an efficient and uniform system of environmental verification in the european union. controls are a very important instrument in the process of implementing and enforcing union law, but member states give controls different political priorities. i therefore fully support the european commission's proposal to amend the existing recommendations in order to improve their effectiveness. i agree with the proposal to include legally binding requirements for the control of individual installations and activities in sectoral legislation. this will allow greater political priority to be given to controls and better enforcement of environmental law throughout the community.

in writing. small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are crucial to the european economy, affecting its competitiveness and employment. by providing over 100 million jobs, smes contribute to economic growth. they are also a major source of regional development, innovation and gender equality. smes in the union continue to have lower productivity and slower growth than smes in the united states, where companies increase employment by an average of 60% in the first seven years of operation, compared to only around 10-20% in europe. the small business charter presented by the european commission in june this year sets out for the first time a comprehensive policy framework for smes, providing a level playing field and improving their legal and administrative environment in the eu. in this context, the urgent question is whether the council intends to formally endorse the charter for small enterprises and whether there will be a binding commitment by member states to comply with its principles. it is important to know what measures the council intends to take to ensure that smes have sustainable access to finance in the context of the financial market crisis.

member of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank the european parliament and in particular the two rapporteurs, josé manuel garcía-margallo y marfil and bart staes, for the constructive reports they have presented on the sensitive subject of the fight against vat fraud in the european union, particularly with regard to the first concrete commission proposal in this field. today we are at a turning point in the implementation of our strategy to combat vat fraud. the three reports which parliament is due to adopt tomorrow contain a number of recommendations on how to improve the fight against fraud and reflect your view on the first of a long series of measures. on 1 december the commission adopted a communication setting out the measures it will be presenting in the coming months and a first directive containing some of these measures. the proposals also address the concerns and recommendations expressed in mr staes' report. the measures which the commission intends to adopt can be divided into three categories: the first group includes measures to prevent vat fraud. one of these is to establish minimum standards for registration and deletion in national databases in order to improve the reliability and comparability of information contained in these databases. the procedure for obtaining electronic confirmation of operators' vat numbers and corresponding names and addresses is also to be improved to provide greater legal certainty for suppliers. the commission also proposes to simplify the rules on invoicing and to streamline the rules on the eligibility of the tax in order to ensure better enforcement, which will facilitate checks. the second category concerns measures to improve the efficiency of tax administrations in detecting vat fraud. the measure on reducing delays, which is the subject of two reports by mr josé manuel garcía-margallo y marfil, falls into this category. to improve fraud detection, it is also necessary to ensure better monitoring of import vat exemptions, as proposed by the commission last monday, and to extend the range of information that member states will have to make available to the tax administrations of other member states through automated access to their databases. finally, this category also includes the creation of a european network, as you have pointed out, called eurofisc, intended to strengthen operational cooperation between the member states in the fight against vat fraud, like the eurocanet network created by the belgian tax administration and supported by the commission and the european anti-fraud office. the third category includes measures to strengthen the capacity of tax administrations to collect and recover taxes. in particular, it contains a measure specifying the cases in which the supplier and the customer of cross-border transactions are jointly and severally liable for the payment of the tax. the legislative framework governing crossborder recovery is likely to be strengthened. finally, one measure aims to establish a shared responsibility between member states for the protection of all tax revenues. the commission also notes that parliament has a constant concern for the protection of the financial interests of the european community, since vat fraud also has an impact on the own resources of the european budget. i welcome the support for the proposal for a regulation on mutual administrative assistance in the fight against fraud, and in particular against vat fraud. the commission also welcomes the request by parliament to the council to continue negotiations on this proposal which will provide a detailed framework for the commission and olaf to provide operational and intelligence support to member states in the fight against vat fraud. the positive opinion expressed by parliament in the draft report on the reduction of deadlines and the rapid progress of work on the matter in the council augur well for the more substantial proposals which the commission will adopt in the near future.
author of the draft opinion of the legal affairs committee. - madam president! - what are you doing? the fight against fraud, which has so far been largely a member state responsibility, is a problem that cannot be solved at national level alone. the fight against tax evasion should be conducted in close cooperation between the administrative authorities of the member states and in cooperation with the commission. the proposals for a directive and a regulation which are the subject of this draft are only partly the result of the indications given as priorities by the ecofin council in june 2007. the proposed amendments are mainly aimed at speeding up the collection and exchange of information relating to intra-community transactions by standardising procedures and reducing to one month the period covered by declarations of intra-community transactions and the deadline for the transmission of information on these transactions between member states. the harmonisation of the rules on the chargeability of services will make it possible to carry out an effective control of the information submitted. the obligation on member states to accept vat returns sent electronically will also be a significant simplification. the proposed legislative measures are only the first steps in putting the aforementioned ecofin demands into practice. a detailed assessment of the impact of the new formal obligations on service providers is still lacking and a special report on this issue, especially as regards the administrative costs borne by taxpayers and administrations and the effectiveness of the fight against tax evasion, would be appropriate. in the light of the justified criticism by the court of auditors of the lack of effective administrative cooperation in this area, the european commission should consider increasing its role, in particular in the area of developing analyses and good practice.
madam president! i wanted to look at both the report and the problem from the point of view of fraud, budgetary losses and distortions of competitiveness. the rules of fair competition are simply being broken by tax fraud. i would like to pay particular tribute to the report and to the rapporteur, mr staes, who has produced a very good report. this is one of the few reports where we do not just talk about the amounts, but we indicate by name the member states where these irregularities occur. i would also like to express my appreciation to the court of auditors for having highlighted these two main groups of reasons: firstly, the reasons on the part of the member states, which we could read as a kind of inaction on the part of the council, the inertia of the member states, which could, through actions that would seem simple - timely exchange of information, reliable exchange of information, the will to find the causes of the situation and eliminate them - contribute a great deal to solving the problem. and also the second part, which is important and has not yet been sufficiently expressed here in the commissioner's speech, namely: what can the commission, together with its subordinate agencies such as the directorate-general for taxation and the customs union, the european anti-fraud office, olaf, really do instead of the often bureaucratic translation of 'how much effort we are putting in, but no effect yet'?
in writing. in taking part in the debate on combating tax crimes, i would like to draw attention to the following points. the amount of lost revenue resulting from vat fraud in the individual member states is extremely high and is increasing year by year. for example, in 2005 these losses amounted to some eur 17 billion in germany and in the uk in the 2005/06 tax year to over eur 18 billion. despite the fact that the european union has taken many initiatives to reduce vat fraud, such as eurocanet (exchange of information on companies suspected of vat fraud, unfortunately without the participation of germany, the united kingdom and italy), and the activities of institutions such as europol, eurojust and olaf, the losses from this are clearly increasing year on year. in this context, efforts to create new intergovernmental structures should be abandoned and the role of the european commission as the central coordinator of administrative cooperation between member states in the fight against vat fraud should be strengthened. the new eurofisc mechanism, which is to be a new decentralised network in which member states are to participate on a voluntary basis, is therefore at least debatable.
in writing . the report on combating tax evasion in intra-community transactions is a very important piece of legislation. tax fraud undermines the principle of fair and transparent taxation and simply undermines the basis on which the communities operate. the lower revenues to the union budget mean that we are not able to fully implement policies. the fight against tax fraud is largely a competence of the member states, but they should not act alone. there is a clear need to coordinate cooperation at community level and to strengthen cooperation between member states' administrations and the european commission. given that a major vat reform is a long-term but also very time-consuming action, the report under review decided that conventional measures should be taken. these concern changes in legislation on the liability of taxpayers for failure to submit or incorrect submission of required documents on time, shortening the deadline for obtaining data and rapidly correcting inaccurate data, and speeding up the exchange of information relating to intra-community transactions.
mr. chairman, please! the attempt by the european union to adopt such a development strategy and to impose on the world that a drastic reduction in carbon dioxide emissions from human activities will have a significant impact on cyclical climate change is the greatest utopia of our time. i'll give you a couple of figures that will show the absurdity of this assumption. well, the international energy agency says that a 50% reduction in carbon emissions will cost the world about 45 trillion dollars by 2050, and that money will achieve a temperature reduction of, quote, 0.02 degrees, which is below statistical error, which can have no effect on the cyclical course of climate change. at the same time, it will lead to a sharp decline in the development of human civilization.
mr. chairman, please! we've said almost everything we need to say about climate change and energy. we know that climate change is happening, but we also know that much more warming has already been recorded in the past. we also know that carbon dioxide emissions in nature are largely unrelated to human activities. humans account for only about 4% of carbon dioxide emissions. the main source of co2 is the ocean, which has 50 times more carbon dioxide than the atmosphere. the carbon dioxide emissions of the individual countries are not uniform. a lot of it comes from developing countries like china and india. without reducing emissions in these countries, europe alone cannot solve the problem. nor will restrictions on countries that emit a lot of carbon solve the problem. economies like poland will continue to rely on coal and biofuels for a long time to come. these resources will be the main driving force of their economy. the expected 20% reduction in co2 emissions by 2020 on the proposed rules breaks down these economies. the aim of reducing co2 emissions by up to 80% by 2050 would lead to a collapse of the energy economy not only in poland but also in many other countries and would certainly lead to a total economic disaster. there is therefore a need to deepen the analysis and take protective measures. the bilateral talks between russia and germany, excluding other member states, are certainly not conducive to solving this problem. we need to talk about this together and come to a common solution. i hope that the meeting in poznań and later in copenhagen in 2009 will lead to an agreement and a solution to the problem for the benefit of all.
mr. chairman, please! forcing the european union countries, which produce only 15% of the world's carbon emissions, to adopt the drastic solutions contained in the energy and climate package is a destructive act not only for poland, but for europe and the world. while the countries of the old union reduced their carbon dioxide emissions by about 3%, poland's emissions were reduced by about 30% as a result of industrial destruction and modernisation activities. yet the european union wants further reductions, which is supposed to be a realization of solidarity and burden sharing, and which will surely cause our industry to collapse and enormously increase costs. we are also against the recently imposed ccs directive, which will prevent the use of geothermal energy and the achievement of the 20% renewable energy share in poland. but it could be the cause of an ecological disaster instead of environmental protection. the release of carbon dioxide from the earth's crust can cause the death of living things and tectonic movements and earthquakes.
mr. chairman, please! we're talking about energy and the environment today. the impact of greenhouse gas emissions on climate change is real, although other factors are currently underestimated. i would like to emphasize that action on this matter must be taken globally. because what will be the effect of our radical reductions in emissions if other countries do not? it is simply that european products will become uncompetitive and our markets will be taken over by others who will not introduce such restrictions. it is also necessary to take into account the situation of countries such as poland, whose energy is substantially based on coal. it is noteworthy that these countries have made tremendous progress in reducing their carbon emissions in recent years. the energy and climate package must therefore be prudent, yet supportive and innovative, pro-economic and pro-environmental, secure and forward-looking. this is especially important now that we are experiencing a severe economic downturn.
mr. chairman, please! under the guise of high environmental goals, the richest countries and corporations are pushing a climate package that is hitting the less wealthy countries of the european union. in the face of the global crisis, the mining and energy sectors (including poland) are being attacked at the cost of slowing economic growth and mass redundancies. i am also in favour of reducing co2 emissions in europe and worldwide, but not at any cost. you can't shut down coal plants or mines overnight. it is not too late to work out a wise compromise that will be acceptable to all countries. however, this is only possible if the specificities of national economies are taken into account. otherwise, we're dealing with dictatorship and injustice, and that's not something we should be consenting to.
mr. chairman, please! the problem of climate change is one of the greatest challenges facing humanity. the european union has set out an ambitious plan to reduce carbon emissions by 20% by 2020, improve energy efficiency and increase the share of renewable energy. these intentions show that the union wants to be a world leader in the fight against climate change, but the european union is not an island and cannot act alone. if we don't convince our partners around the world to make equally ambitious adjustments, then despite our best efforts, we may not be able to tackle this problem. the proposed changes should be designed in the most effective way to minimise the costs to the economy, which will be huge anyway, and thus reduce the burden on citizens. in assessing the commission's proposal in this context, i would point out two dangers. first, the need for electricity generating plants to buy emission allowances through auctions will cause a significant increase in energy prices, especially in countries with a high share of coal in energy production. this will have a negative impact on the material situation of households and on the competitiveness of enterprises in these countries. this problem can be partially solved by introducing a benchmarking method. this method gives a premium to the most efficient solutions in its fuel category, thereby achieving the intended reduction target at a significantly lower cost. secondly, the currently proposed allocation system strongly favours industries exposed to carbon leakage at the expense of energy and heating. in effect, it gives the wealthier countries a privileged position, which does not seem to be a fair solution. the allocation system must be designed so that the less prosperous countries do not lose out to the others. the fairest solution seems to be one that divides the auction revenues by gross domestic product. i call on the commission and the council to find a sensible compromise so that the pursuit of these objectives does not lead to the undermining of the competitiveness of our economies and the deterioration of the living conditions of our societies.
mr. chairman, please! the main driver of climate change is the emission of heat from the sun, which provides about 96% of the planet's heat. excessive co2 and methane emissions have a negative impact on the environment and should therefore be reduced. the way out of the impasse is to take radical technical and organisational measures to accelerate the development of renewable energy production, to increase the production of clean electricity, to accelerate all measures to increase energy efficiency and savings. this certainly requires restructuring of expenditure and the mobility of funds for these purposes, but all these actions cannot result in a radical increase in electricity prices. this is something that neither european society nor european industry can accept. therefore, the package in the current entry requires radical refinement.

the next item is the report drawn up on behalf of the committee on regional development by mr stavros arnaoutakis on the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 on the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund as regards certain revenue-generating projects (13874/2008 - c6-0387/2008 - 2008/0186 ((avc)) (a6-0477/2008).
member of the commission. on 15 november, the commission adopted a proposal to revise article 55 of the general regulation on the structural funds, which concerns the conditions for taking account of revenue-generating projects in the context of the cohesion policy programme. the change was purely to simplify administrative procedures. the first practical operations carried out in accordance with the provisions of article 55 revealed serious difficulties in terms of effective implementation. these difficulties, reported by the member states, have revealed a lack of proportionality in the application of the procedures for setting the maximum eligible amount, known as the 'funding gap', and in the monitoring of the project. the aim of the amendment of the regulation in question is to exclude from the application of article 55 all operations co-financed by the european social fund, as well as small-scale projects requiring a total cost of less than eur 1 million co-financed by the european regional development fund and the cohesion fund. the choice of the eur 1 million limit is based on preliminary studies carried out in order to preserve the general nature of article 55. we hope that this simplification, which is a kind of de minimis clause, will enable us to speed up the application of funds to member states and their regions, in particular for the most innovative operations in areas such as research, the promotion of renewable energy sources, etc. it was nevertheless important to avoid legal uncertainty that would have prolonged the admission procedure disproportionately. such uncertainty could have led project managers to suspend the implementation of operational programmes, which had to be avoided at all costs. in view of this, the commission decided to propose only one amendment of a technical nature. this choice was a success, as thanks to the work of the council and the parliamentary committees on regional development and employment, we were able to complete the review process in just 3 months. on behalf of the commission, may i sincerely thank your rapporteur, mr arnaoutakis. i hope that, thanks to our fruitful cooperation, the european parliament will give its consent to allow the review to be completed by the end of the year and to allow the managing authorities to continue their work, which is the strength of this simplification. the article 55 review also demonstrated the quality of the work carried out in cooperation between the regional policy dg and the employment dg, which is a benefit to cohesion policy. this cooperation never wavered. this is demonstrated by the fact that, as part of the european economic recovery plan, commissioner hübner and i have joined forces to propose three new substantial amendments to the structural funds regulation, which you will also be discussing.
on behalf of the ppe-de group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the regulation is very short and concise, but it is very important. this meaning is related to the context in which the change takes place. first, by making this change, the european institutions show that they are able to respond flexibly to the difficulties encountered in implementing a particular policy. the willingness to make the action easier and simpler for the beneficiaries indicates that the european commission, followed by the european parliament and the council, are indeed prepared to adapt the rules to the real conditions. secondly, the importance of this regulation also lies in the fact that we are dealing with an amendment of the regulation during the programming period. this is extremely important because this is not the last change and the way the debate on the regulation change will be conducted will be very important from the point of view of preparing the crisis-related corrective package. thirdly, the european commission has been criticised on many occasions for its control of expenditure, and the court of auditors' criticism was essentially that the procedures were too complex. today's regulation shows that bold and decisive action is needed to improve efficiency and to show that european money can be spent quickly, efficiently and effectively.
on behalf of the uen group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. although the european parliament resolution under discussion today is essentially formal, technical, it touches on important issues relating to the use of eu aid. the proposed regulation concerns article 55 of the council regulation laying down general provisions on the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund. the current fifth paragraph, which refers to eur 200 000 as the maximum cost of the monitoring procedure, is replaced by a provision stating that the rules on revenue-generating projects will only apply to those operations which are financed by the european regional development fund or the cohesion fund, provided that their cost does not exceed eur 1 million. so i ask you: is this amount enough, or is it too high, or is it too low? i am convinced that this will avoid unnecessary bureaucratic red tape for a large group of smaller operations. this should make the management of projects, which often involve local and regional authorities, and which concern environmental protection, innovation, energy, etc., more operational. for example, in poland we have over 100 different types of institutions managing the implementation of eu funds. the efficiency of their work depends on the speed with which they are able to use the aid. i also hope that this initiative will lead to further simplifications, as the commissioner has been kind enough to mention. on behalf of the uen group, i would like to thank you for your creative approach to legislation that allows the most rational use of eu funds.
mr. chairman, please! in the debate on the amendment of the council regulations relating to the structural funds, i would like to draw attention to four points. first, the legal rules governing the use of funds from the european regional development fund, the cohesion fund or the european social fund are often so complex that they discourage the use of these funds or make it difficult to implement projects and to settle them. secondly, it is therefore a good thing that the european commission has proposed to amend article 55 of the regulation, by excluding from the scope of that article, inter alia, projects financed by the european social fund which are likely to generate income. this change should facilitate activities such as social inclusion projects and care services. thirdly, the application of article 5 of the regulation to small projects co-financed by the european regional development fund and the cohesion fund has also been restricted as regards the calculation of the maximum amount of eligible expenditure and the monitoring of these projects. moreover, all these changes are to apply retroactively from 1 august 2006. fourthly, all these proposals are positive examples of how the rules on the structural funds can be simplified effectively in order to make them more efficient, which i believe is in the interest of both the beneficiaries and all the citizens of the european union.
mr. chairman, please! for small projects co-financed by the european regional development fund and the cohesion fund and for operations co-financed by the european social fund, the monitoring mechanisms in place, under which revenues may be taken into account even after three years from the closure of the operational programme, are clearly too much of an administrative burden, disproportionate to the amounts involved and a significant risk factor for the implementation of those programmes. the commission therefore rightly considers that it is important and necessary to adopt amendments to article 55 (5) of regulation no 1083/2006. the aim of these amendments is to simplify effectively the existing rules on the structural funds in the interest and for the benefit of citizens in important areas such as the environment, social inclusion, research, competitiveness and energy. i want to say that today, in the midst of the economic and financial crisis, great efforts are being made in poland to ensure that the structural funds are used as quickly as possible, that the amounts are paid out as quickly as possible. this is one of the opportunities, especially for the new member states, to counter the economic crisis. the structural funds must be used quickly and efficiently.

2005/29 on unfair business-to-consumer commercial practices and regulation (ec) 2006/2004 on consumer protection cooperation, does not apply. however, some form of protection is offered by directive from which the companies operate to decide, on a case-by-case basis, whether a commercial communication is misleading and to take appropriate enforcement measures. i would also like to point out that commercial practices directive does not cover business-to-business commercial practices because there is no case for maximum harmonisation of national laws on unfair competition. a comprehensive harmonisation directive on unfair business-to-consumer practices was already a very ambitious proposal which would have failed if its scope had been extended to unfair business-to-consumer competition practices. the consultation leading up to the proposal and the work in the council have shown that there is little support for extending the scope of the directive to unfair business-to-business commercial practices. while some member states were in favour of extending the scope of the directive and unfair competition acts, others expressed support for consumer protection but opposed the establishment at eu level of a harmonised complementary system of unfair competition rules. although the commission cannot take action against companies involved in such practices, it has endeavoured to raise awareness of the problem among companies by presenting it to various european trade organisations. the issue has been raised in particular within the business support network and, at the same time, the small business act requires member states to protect small and medium-sized enterprises from unfair practices. if it deems it appropriate, the commission will continue to examine other ways of raising awareness among businesses. in addition, the commission wrote to the competent authorities of the member states concerned spain, austria and germany to draw their attention to the fact that the situation persists and to request further information. the responses received clearly show that the national authorities are aware of the problem and have legislation in place to deal with it; where appropriate, they have already made use of the measures provided for.

in writing. the current debate on the 'green package' confirms the ambitious goals europe is setting in the fight against climate change. the automotive industry is part of the european strategy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 20%, reduce the energy consumption of the economy and increase the share of energy from renewable sources by 2020 compared to 1990. this is particularly relevant for co2 reduction activities. according to eu figures, cars currently account for 12% of total emissions of this gas in the community. the high level of emissions is mainly due to the increasing number of cars and the increased use of road transport, which is not offset by improvements in engine design or reductions in vehicle weight. the reduction of the co2 emission limit for passenger cars to 120 grams per kilometre by 2012 and the establishment of a long-term strategy to reduce this limit to 95 grams per kilometre by 2020 takes into account the european parliament's proposal that the development of new types of passenger cars takes between 5 and 7 years, which consequently affects the development and production cycles of the automotive industry. the assumptions adopted should be considered environmentally ambitious. on the other hand, the increased r & d costs imposed by the new standards promote scientific research into fuel-saving technologies. this increases the level of innovation in the automotive sector, which in turn will support the competitiveness of the european economy.

in writing. i am understandably interested in the work of frontex, as it is the only eu institution located in poland. contrary to earlier concerns about the tightness of the eastern border of the european union, the main threats to illegal immigration have emerged in the mediterranean. this is therefore the main area of operation of frontex. i had the opportunity to visit malta and the camps for african refugees there, so i understand the gravity of the problem and the immense human suffering that lies in the desperate sea crossing towards malta and the continental shores of the european union. illegal immigration is a common challenge and requires a common strategy and community tools. these tools have been developed by frontex since october 2005 and the eurosur border surveillance system. understanding the growing financial needs, the european parliament is seeking an increase in the budget of the frontex agency for the third year in a row. the member states' commitment to this matter and the distribution of financial, equipment and operational burdens has been highly uneven. for geographical reasons and therefore different sensitivities to the problem of immigration, the uneven involvement of the european community actors in this community policy seems to be a permanent feature, difficult to overcome.
in writing. in view of the risks posed by illegal immigration, europe needs more integrated management of the union's borders through a harmonised approach to migration, including the organisation of legal immigration. even if it were assumed that each member state should control its own border, given the situation on both the eastern and southern borders, appropriate cooperation should be undertaken in order to share material and human resources to combat this phenomenon. the appropriate introduction of border controls will reduce cross-border crime and thereby contribute to raising the level of internal security. in addition to its activities aimed at reducing the flow of illegal immigrants, frontex should also promote the strengthening of the global partnership with third countries and make some progress in the area of the right to asylum. illegal immigration is also characterised by a high number of deaths that occur when crossing borders illegally. this should be the case for the establishment of year-round patrols in high-risk areas to monitor the risk of loss of life. it is necessary to establish two separate units, one of which should monitor the land border and the other the sea border, paying particular attention to the use of the overland routes by migrants along the eastern border. there is also a strong need for continued training of staff involved in frontex activities to increase their efficiency and professionalism, and for a common system of information exchange to optimise activities.
madam president! we are not here to be convinced of the dangers of counterfeiting. there are many cases where counterfeits have endangered health or even life, and there is no need to go into detail here. it is enough to mention that not only luxury goods, cds, but also medicines, foodstuffs for children and adults, and car parts are counterfeited, often endangering our safety and causing losses not only to small and medium-sized enterprises. the counterfeiters are organized into criminal groups. their activities are highly profitable and must be combated. this is why joint ventures are needed, not just in the area of customs activities, but also strong administrative cooperation between member states, which in my view is currently insufficient. only the european commission's action against the smuggling of counterfeit cigarettes is a positive example of such cooperation. i would like to see this experience transferred to the fight against other counterfeit products. the issue of counterfeiting is the responsibility of several directorates-general of the european commission. it might be a good idea to designate a single directorate-general within the commission responsible for these matters and to define the scope of its competence. a written declaration on similar products, prepared by me and others, is now before the european parliament. many original products are copied by so-called similar products. it is often unclear to what extent similar products can be prosecuted for infringement of laws on unfair competition or intellectual property rights. moreover, consumers often buy similar products mistaking them for branded products. it is difficult to estimate the scale of the problem in the european market. i would therefore like to have the european commission reply to the question whether it intends to accede to our request and prepare studies on the impact and status of similar products on the internal market.
madam president! there is no doubt that counterfeiting and piracy have recently become a major problem in international trade. the european union, the world's second largest importer, is particularly vulnerable to counterfeit goods, from branded products, toys and medicines, mainly from asian countries. it should be noted that this phenomenon has a much wider scope and more serious consequences than we think. products supplied to the european market in breach of intellectual property rights are generally of lower quality and, consequently, also much cheaper than their original counterparts. this in turn leads the consumer to prefer the former for economic reasons. counterfeiting and piracy are theft, and i fully support any initiative to curb this practice. i am particularly concerned about the intensity of the violence we have seen recently. we must therefore take decisive action not only at european level but also within the wto. let's not let this robbery go unpunished.
the next item is the joint debate on the report drawn up by ieke van den burg on behalf of the committee on legal affairs on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending council directives 78/660/eec and 83/349/eec as regards certain disclosure requirements for medium-sized enterprises and the preparation of consolidated accounts (com2008) 0195 - c6-0173/2008 - 2008/0084 (cod)) (a6-0462/2008), and the commission statement on the accounting obligations of medium-sized enterprises.
mr. chairman, please! the main objective of entrepreneurship policy is to create an environment favourable to the creation and development of enterprises. the improvement of the economic environment includes administrative and legal simplifications and financial, tax, social and environmental impacts that affect the activities of enterprises. the unification of regulations brings enormous benefits to the entire international business environment. first, financial reporting standards of transnational relevance facilitate the assessment and comparison of the financial situation of companies from different countries and thereby facilitate investment decision-making. second, by preparing financial statements in accordance with generally recognised and accepted accounting principles, companies have a wider access to capital. smes are often subject to the same rules as large companies, but their specific accounting needs are rarely examined. it is important that discussions focus not only on simplification but also on the relevance of financial reporting requirements for small and medium-sized enterprises as opposed to large listed companies. the debate on simplification is generally focused on costs. the debate on the significance of the requirements is about the benefits of financial reporting and about the individual users and their needs. there are several reasons for introducing simplified rules for smes. first, the benefits of implementing global standards in small and medium-sized non-public companies are certainly less than in large publicly traded companies. this leads to a mismatch between the benefits and costs of applying standards. the establishment of an appropriate cost-benefit ratio requires the reduction of the latter. secondly, financial reporting does not play a significant role in meeting the information needs of sme owners, as they have direct access to the information. thirdly, users of financial statements of smes are generally less knowledgeable about reporting accounting and should therefore be adapted to the capabilities of the recipients.
mr. chairman, please! the european parliament has for many years been sounding the alarm about the problem of unnecessary and disproportionately high administrative costs imposed on european businesses. it is therefore gratifying that the commission has finally addressed this issue by proposing, by means of an accelerated procedure, amendments to the fourth and seventh company law directives as regards disclosure requirements for medium-sized enterprises and the obligation to prepare consolidated accounts. i support the commission's approach to simplifying the conditions for european businesses to operate, but on the assumption that these changes will not result in a reduction in transparency and a loss of information for account users. the proposal to remove the requirement to disclose the organisation's costs also seems appropriate. extension to medium-sized enterprises of the exemptions for small enterprises, which are already widely used in most member states, could help to reduce the reporting burden for the former. as regards the proposed amendments to the seventh company law directive, the requirement to draw up separate financial statements is not in fact justified by the fact that consolidated accounts would in this case be virtually identical to optional individual accounts. the european commission should continue its efforts to amend the fourth and seventh company law directives with a view to presenting a european accounting framework before the end of 2009. uniform standards will reduce the administrative burden for smes and increase transparency for all actors involved.
mr. chairman, please! small and medium-sized enterprises in the european union employ about 60% of the workforce. so their economic condition is very important. in particular, in times of financial crisis, it is important not to complicate their legal obligations in order to facilitate their activities. this is an opportunity for these companies and their employees. the reporting simplifications provided for in the amending directive are a step in the right direction. however, i agree with a colleague who pointed out the need to ensure that local journalists have access to information.
president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all, i am sorry for the delay. we were late leaving paris. although i did not hear all the debates, i also wanted to thank you for the debate today. the council takes note and will take note of each of your comments and recommendations and of your interest in these matters, particularly as regards your commitment to simplifying the burden on business. this is a very sensitive issue today, but we must, particularly in the context of the crisis, simplify without deregulation to build a much safer environment in europe, to ensure the development of small and mediumsized enterprises.
the commission's vice-president - mr president, i welcome the minister and, like her, i would like to join in the thanks that have been addressed to parliament, to mrs van den burg, to mr lehne and to mr gauzès for having carried out this work which has enabled us today to reach this first provision. i have heard what has been said about small businesses. the aim is to adapt the rules for small businesses when the revision is planned, but i would like to reiterate that member states will have the choice either to use these rules or to create another alternative adapted to local circumstances. i have personally been very sensitive to the argument that small businesses should not be relegated to a situation which, under the pretext of simplification, would put them somewhat outside the realm of economic life. i believe that this debate will enlighten my colleague, mr mccreevy, who is responsible for the internal market, and that it will enable us to continue to reduce the administrative burden on businesses, especially the smallest ones. we thank parliament for its continued support and hope that this good cooperation will continue in the new year.

the next item on the agenda is the joint debate on the report drawn up by mr manuel medina ortega on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, containing recommendations to the commission on the european official journal (2008/2124 (ini)) (a6-0451/2008), the report drawn up by ms diana wallis on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, on recommendations to the commission on e-justice (2008/2125 (ini)) (a6-0467/2008), and the report drawn up by mr antonio lópeza-istúriza white on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, on recommendations to the commission on the legal protection of adults: cross-border implications (2008/2123 (ini)) (a6-0460/2008).
on behalf of the uen group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. we're discussing three very important reports. i would like to thank in particular mrs wallis for her extremely comprehensive, substantive, competent, excellent and all-embracing report. the european parliament, followed by mrs wallis, stresses the importance of the problem affecting at least 2% of the citizens of the member states of the european union. of the nearly 500 million inhabitants of the european union, 10 million are involved in international litigation. for these people, the use of the latest information systems in the area of justice can be crucial, it can improve, simplify and shorten the time of court proceedings. our proposals, whether they are taken up by the european commission, can facilitate access to justice and, importantly for our citizens, reduce the cost of litigation. there seems to be reasonable support for the idea of two e-justice web portals. the first would serve citizens, including businesses, by providing legal aid - legal advice in many languages. the second, the sectoral, professional one, would be an instrument to assist lawyers, judges, prosecutors or advocates and judicial officers in their work. new technologies can also be used to combat transnational crime and for prevention. not to mention the proliferation of videoconferencing as a natural method of obtaining and collecting evidence in ongoing cases.
mr. chairman, please! the european union must address the significant ageing of the populations of the member states associated with a significant increase in life expectancy. so the number of people aged over 60 will be about 40% of the european population by 2050, with over 10% of our population being over 80. these demographic changes have serious economic, social, health and budgetary implications. this requires the establishment of appropriate and specific safeguards guaranteeing equal rights and obligations in all areas. increasingly, protected persons are staying in a country other than their country of residence or receiving hospital treatment in a country other than the country in which their assets are located. legal protection systems therefore need to ensure the continuity of judicial decisions, administrative decisions or decisions taken by the protected person himself. this is particularly the case for the future protection powers which must be used in the member states of the union. it is therefore necessary to provide for an effective mechanism for the transmission of files, in particular in cases of urgency, where, for example, a person subject to a protection measure needs to be hospitalised while temporarily staying outside his or her country of origin. this would allow europeans to travel or reside in a member state other than their country of origin without any obstacles, without losing access to effective and rapid treatment.
mr. chairman, please! in its communication to the parliament and the council of 10 may 2005 on the hague programme, the commission identified as a specific priority the guarantee of a genuine european area in civil justice with regard to the recognition and enforcement of judgments and the implementation by 2011 of the principle of mutual recognition, which is a concrete measure for the protection of citizens across borders in europe. the union is growing, and citizens are encouraged to move more and more. however, the circulation of these documents within the community is hampered by problems relating to the circulation of official documents. the different approaches adopted by the member states to the recognition of authentic instruments originating in other countries have resulted in the current flow of these instruments being problematic, limited both in number and in the types of instruments. it is necessary for the commission to take concrete steps to introduce without delay a single system of mutual recognition and enforcement, appropriate for official acts and common to all member states, which will greatly facilitate the daily lives of citizens and businesses. at the same time, given the differences in the structure and organisation of public ownership and property register systems, entries in public property registers should not be covered by that abolition. the authenticity of an authentic instrument shall be subject to the conditions laid down in article 4 of this regulation. finally, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr manuel medina ortedz, on a very well-written document.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to start by congratulating ms. diana wallis on her excellent report and draw your attention to two facts. as chairman of the committee on petitions, i have observed how often citizens of the european union are not aware of the rights they have, and on the other hand sometimes they think they can intervene in matters where they have no rights. the european parliament has also launched a new website, the e-justice portal, which will help eu citizens to contact the european parliament and its committee on petitions. i also wanted to draw attention to the second thing that ms. diana wallis said in her speech: you have to respect local laws. this was said 250 years ago by the famous french philosopher montesquieu, who said that when you make laws at a higher level, at the territorial level, you should always remember that small districts, small territories, and in this case the states of the european union, have their own traditions that must be respected.
mr. chairman, please! in each member state we have different legal systems, different rules on the admissibility of acts. we should therefore strive to make the cross-border movement of official documents as easy as possible, but we must remember that the certainty and security of legal situations and activities is more important than the ease of movement. the rules on the recognition of official acts need to be harmonised to make life easier for our citizens and to simplify the way businesses operate, as they expect. such rules will certainly save time and money. we must strive to establish uniform rules for the recognition of authentic instruments in the various member states, but the category of authentic instruments should certainly not be extended to those documents which do not meet the essential requirements.
