in writing. − the european parliament's december session voted on the european action plan on employment mobility prepared by the committee on employment and social affairs. labour mobility is based on the fundamental principle of free movement of persons within the internal market in accordance with the treaty establishing the european community. security is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the citizens of the european union. community legislation should protect migrant workers against the loss of their social protection. significant progress has been made in this area, but efforts should continue to reduce administrative and legal obstacles to mobility caused by the specificities of the rules in each member state. it is employment mobility that is the means of strengthening the economic and social dimension of the lisbon strategy. mobility appears to be a necessary means to achieve the objectives of the renewed european social agenda and to address a number of challenges such as demographic change, globalisation and technological progress. i support the european mobility action plan, including the idea of an information and advice portal providing advice on all aspects of occupational mobility - including job vacancies, healthcare and social security, recognition of qualifications and training.
in writing. the european parliament has adopted a directive on the safety of toys. it is a very good directive that increases the safety of toys that end up in the hands of our children. this is particularly important at a time when we are increasingly hearing about accidents that have been caused by toys, for example by swallowing parts that are not properly fitted. it is worth noting that a large proportion (around 80%) of toys on the european market are imported from china. the directive has succeeded in reconciling the interests of groups representing the interests of consumers and of representatives of the toy industry. i can only rejoice that a compromise has been reached on a regulation so crucial to me as a parent. both groups benefit from this directive. consumers can be sure that toys that reach the european market and are offered to their children meet high safety standards, are free of harmful substances and carry clear warnings for those buying toys. the toy industry has repeatedly stressed that the safety of children is not subject to any compromise, hence their favourable position to the proposed changes. however, these changes should not jeopardise the position of european toy companies. the negotiated agreement will give them an additional two years to adapt to the new chemicals legislation.
in writing. − improving vocational training is a key element in achieving the lisbon strategy's objectives of economic growth, competitiveness, employment and social cohesion. the planned european credit transfer and accumulation system for vocational education and training (ecvet) is one of the initiatives in the field of education at european level. learning outcomes vary considerably due to the diversity of national vocational education and training systems. ecvet provides a methodological framework that covers acquired knowledge, skills and competences, organises the issue of transfer and accumulation of points and places them in the context of qualifications. it facilitates cross-border labour mobility and transparency of professional qualifications acquired abroad. ecvet can be a valuable instrument for adapting vocational education and training systems to labour market requirements, provided that it takes into account national and regional specificities and is functional from the point of view of its users - workers and enterprises, including smes and smaller establishments in europe. it supports cross-border mobility as well as access to lifelong learning in vocational education and training. it should enable learners to choose their own career. i believe that the introduction of ecvet will make an important contribution to the creation of a european labour market, provided that the administrative burden associated with it is reduced.
in writing. − the report by ieke van den burg on the amendment of certain disclosure requirements for medium-sized enterprises and the obligation to prepare consolidated financial statements is a good piece of legislation. the report presented by the legal affairs committee aims to simplify the conditions for doing business for medium-sized european companies in the short term. it consists primarily in exempting them from the obligation to disclose information on the costs of the organisation as assets (i.e. costs associated with the establishment of the company) and to prepare consolidated financial statements by parent companies with only non-significant subsidiaries. i am of the opinion that the extension to medium-sized enterprises of the exemptions for small enterprises in the context of the harmonisation of company law does not threaten to reduce transparency, but on the contrary may considerably reduce the financial and administrative burden on small enterprises.
